raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Problem

LayerNorm / RMSNorm backward rows whose width has no whole-warp vector mapping take the plain one-CTA-per-row `_ln_bwd_kernel`: in bf16 / fp16 that is every width that is not a multiple of 64 (48, 96, 200, 720, 1000, 2000, 3000, ...). Its dgamma / dbeta are per-element fp32 atomics straight into the `[C]` outputs, so all R rows serialize on the same C addresses. On a B300 the backward at C = 96 takes 0.55 ms at 65k rows and 1.09 ms at 131k rows, where the native backend takes about 0.15 ms.

## Change

- `_ln_bwd_kernel` takes an `nslots` constexpr (default 0: unchanged). With `nslots > 0`, row r adds into slot `r % nslots` of a `[nslots, C]` fp32 partial buffer. The existing `_ln_bwd_finalize_kernel` then sums the slots into dgamma / dbeta (`_ln_bwd_slots_host`).
- The plain route of `backward()` uses it from 1024 rows. `nslots` is `min(1024, R // 16, 2^21 // C)` rounded down to a power of two: it is part of the compile key, so it takes at most five values (64 ... 1024) instead of changing with every row count. The partials are carved from the workspace, and `scratch_bytes` reports them.
- dgamma / dbeta stay atomic reductions, so they are no more bitwise repeatable run to run than before. Only the summation order changes; dx is unaffected.
- Below 1024 rows the direct atomics stay. The pipelined, tiled and CGA routes and the extended-affine backward are unchanged. The forward is untouched.

## Measurements (B300, cc 10.3)

Both legs run `benchmark/norms/_norm_bench_worker.py --backend cudnn` with the default plan (the FROST engine), each in its own process: develop, then this branch, with the order alternating per cell. The ratio is this branch's backward time over develop's.

- **Training grid** (bf16, LayerNorm / RMSNorm, rows 1024-131072 x C 96 / 160 / 1000 / 2000 / 5000): 0.100-0.902. The forward, which this change does not touch, measured 0.984-1.018.
- **Row floor.** A first version without a floor failed its frozen holdout at 201 rows (1.187: the extra launch). A small-row grid (rows 64-1024, C 96 / 720 / 2000, bf16 / fp16) gave:
  - 1.07-1.34 up to 256 rows;
  - 0.77-1.11 at 512 rows;
  - 0.53-0.91 at 1024 rows.

  Hence the 1024-row floor.
- **Frozen holdout.** The rule was fixed before the draw, with the criterion "every cell <= 1.03x develop". The draw was 16 cells: off-grid widths 48-6000, rows log-uniform from 1024 to 200k, bf16 and fp16. Range 0.097-0.752:

| norm | rows | C | dtype | develop µs | this branch µs | ratio |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| LayerNorm | 95156 | 48 | bf16 | 610.9 | 59.4 | 0.097 |
| RMSNorm | 2977 | 480 | fp16 | 30.5 | 14.3 | 0.470 |
| LayerNorm | 3208 | 720 | bf16 | 36.9 | 17.2 | 0.466 |
| RMSNorm | 1084 | 3000 | fp16 | 26.8 | 17.5 | 0.653 |
| LayerNorm | 4810 | 720 | bf16 | 49.6 | 22.0 | 0.444 |
| RMSNorm | 132340 | 3000 | fp16 | 1265.1 | 663.9 | 0.525 |
| LayerNorm | 12278 | 200 | fp16 | 108.2 | 29.1 | 0.269 |
| RMSNorm | 32731 | 1500 | bf16 | 587.2 | 153.2 | 0.261 |
| LayerNorm | 25517 | 6000 | bf16 | 514.8 | 277.1 | 0.538 |
| RMSNorm | 22150 | 3000 | bf16 | 225.2 | 128.9 | 0.572 |
| LayerNorm | 17162 | 200 | bf16 | 148.5 | 38.1 | 0.256 |
| RMSNorm | 26274 | 48 | bf16 | 91.5 | 22.0 | 0.240 |
| LayerNorm | 2063 | 200 | bf16 | 22.4 | 10.4 | 0.464 |
| RMSNorm | 198740 | 480 | bf16 | 1694.9 | 406.9 | 0.240 |
| LayerNorm | 5054 | 48 | bf16 | 37.9 | 10.9 | 0.287 |
| RMSNorm | 20480 | 6000 | bf16 | 278.1 | 209.2 | 0.752 |

**Power-of-two slot counts (6890c11f).** The first head used `R // 16` directly. That compiled a new artifact for each row count between 1024 and 16k rows. The fix rounds the count down to a power of two. I re-measured the same 16 holdout cells afterwards, so this is not a fresh holdout. The ratios were 0.096-0.750, against 0.097-0.752 before.

The same holdout also covered an extension of the slots to the extended-affine backward (zero-centered gamma / adaptive), which reuses this kernel. Three of its 16 cells exceeded 1.03: 1.14-1.40, at 2.5k-5.6k rows per address with C 1536-4096. That extension is not part of this PR.

The kernel path is architecture-independent, so cc 10.0 takes the same change. I measured only on cc 10.3.

## Tests

- New `test/python/norm/cutedsl/test_frost_norm_plain_backward_slots.py`: dx / dgamma / dbeta against an fp64 reference on both sides of the 1024-row floor, for LayerNorm and RMSNorm in bf16 and fp16, with stale caller buffers.
- On B300, against develop with only this change applied: `test_frost_norm_affine`, `test_frost_norm_plain_backward_slots`, `test_frost_norm_small_c_backward`, `test_frost_norm_no_alloc`, `test_layernorm`, `test_rmsnorm`, `test_frost_norm_engines`, `test_frost_norm_engine_e2e` and `test_norm_fuzzer` gave 1232 passed, 1 skipped. At 6890c11f, the whole of `test/python/norm` gave 1358 passed, 1 skipped.

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+"""LN/RMS backward on the plain route with its dgamma / dbeta spread over slots.
+
+Rows whose width has no whole-warp vector mapping (C not a multiple of 64 in bf16 / fp16) take the plain one-CTA-per-row
+backward, whose dgamma / dbeta are atomics. From 1024 rows those atomics go to a [nslots, C] partial buffer that the
+finalize kernel sums; this checks every gradient on both sides of the threshold against an fp64 reference.
+
+    pytest test/python/norm/cutedsl/test_frost_norm_plain_backward_slots.py
+"""
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+pytest.importorskip("cudnn.norm", reason="frost norm kernels require a built cudnn frontend")
+
+from cudnn.norm._lazy import dsl_unavailable  # noqa: E402
+
+requirement_error = dsl_unavailable("FROST norm tests")
+if requirement_error:
+    pytest.skip(requirement_error, allow_module_level=True)
+
+from cudnn.norm import NormVariant, norm_bprop, norm_fprop  # noqa: E402
+from cudnn.norm.bprop.kernels.layernorm_sm100 import _bwd_pipe_cfg, _plain_bwd_slots  # noqa: E402
+
+_EB = {torch.bfloat16: 2, torch.float16: 2}
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L0
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("variant", [NormVariant.LAYER_NORM, NormVariant.RMS_NORM], ids=["layer_norm", "rms_norm"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("dtype", [torch.bfloat16, torch.float16], ids=["bf16", "fp16"])
+@pytest.mark.parametrize("rows, cols", [(16, 96), (1000, 96), (40000, 96), (5000, 80), (8192, 160), (3000, 1000), (2048, 2000)])
+def test_plain_route_gradients(variant, dtype, rows, cols):
+    if not torch.cuda.is_available() or torch.cuda.get_device_capability() not in ((10, 0), (10, 3)):
+        pytest.skip("the SM100 norm kernels need compute capability 10.0 or 10.3")
+    assert _bwd_pipe_cfg(cols, _EB[dtype]) is None or _bwd_pipe_cfg(cols, _EB[dtype])[3] < 2, "not a plain-route width"
+    assert bool(_plain_bwd_slots(rows, cols)) == (rows >= 1024), "the case sits on the wrong side of the slot threshold"
+    has_beta = variant is NormVariant.LAYER_NORM
+    torch.manual_seed(763)
+    x = torch.randn(rows, cols, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+    g = torch.randn(cols, device="cuda", dtype=dtype)
+    b = torch.randn(cols, device="cuda", dtype=dtype) if has_beta else None
+    dy = torch.randn_like(x)
+
+    _, mean, rstd = norm_fprop(variant, x, g, b, eps=1e-5, normalized_shape=[cols])
+    # stale bytes in the caller's buffers: the route must clear them itself
+    out = tuple(torch.full(s, 7.0, device="cuda", dtype=dt) for s, dt in (((rows, cols), dtype), ((cols,), torch.float32), ((cols,), torch.float32)))
+    dx, dgamma, dbeta = norm_bprop(variant, dy, x, g, mean, rstd, has_beta=has_beta, normalized_shape=[cols], out=out if has_beta else out[:2] + (None,))
+    torch.cuda.synchronize()
+
+    xr = x.double().detach().requires_grad_(True)
+    gr = g.double().detach().requires_grad_(True)
+    br = b.double().detach().requires_grad_(True) if has_beta else None
+    yr = F.layer_norm(xr, [cols], gr, br, 1e-5) if has_beta else F.rms_norm(xr, [cols], gr, eps=1e-5)
+    ref = torch.autograd.grad(yr, [t for t in (xr, gr, br) if t is not None], dy.double())
+    pairs = [("dx", dx, ref[0]), ("dgamma", dgamma, ref[1])] + ([("dbeta", dbeta, ref[2])] if has_beta else [])
+    for what, got, want in pairs:
+        err = (got.double() - want).abs().max().item() / max(1.0, want.abs().max().item())
+        assert err <= 3e-2, f"{what}: rel {err:.2e}"
+
+
+@pytest.mark.L0
+def test_plain_route_slot_count_does_not_follow_every_row_count():
+    """The slot count is a compile-key value: it must not change with each new row count (one JIT compile per batch)."""
+    counts = {_plain_bwd_slots(rows, 96) for rows in range(1024, 70000, 37)}
+    assert counts <= {64, 128, 256, 512, 1024}, counts
+    assert _plain_bwd_slots(2050, 96) == _plain_bwd_slots(3333, 96)
